فَرْثٌ The سِرْجِين [here meaning feces] (S, A, O, K) while remaining (S, O) in the كَرِش [or stomach of a ruminant animal]; (S, A, O, K;) the dregs in the كرش: (Jel in xvi. 68:) or i. q. سِرْقِين [a dial. var. of سرجين]: and the سرقين of the كرش; as also ↓ فُرَاثَةٌ , (M,) [i. e.] الفُرَاثَةُ signifies what is extracted from the كرش [like
الفَرْثُ: it is erroneously expl. in the K: see 4]: (O:) the pl. of فَرْثٌ is فُرُوثٌ. (S, O.) ―
-b2- And Anything that is scattered from a bag or other receptacle for travelling-provisions &c. (M.) ＝
-A2- Also A small [leathern vessel for water, of the kind called] رَكْوَة [q. v.]; (T, K;) a dial. var. of قَرْثُ: (K:) or the small رَكْوَة is called القَرْثُ [only], with ق. (O.) ＝
-A3- See also the last of the following paragraphs.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
